variants.label: Good wireless router, strong signal (the wiki's upper HEVC range)
Average Wi-Fi or a busy network (the wiki's lower HEVC range)

notes: Starting point compiled from public guidance, NOT verified by the AirFrameXR project on this headset (no `verified` entry). AirFrameXR's support for headsets other than the Apple Vision Pro is best effort.

Same reasoning as the Quest profiles: Pico's ALVR client is the same Android client as the Quest's and the Pico 4 / 4 Ultra use a Qualcomm Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 like the Quest 3 (Pico's specification). 90 Hz, HEVC 10-bit (the default session forces it; ALVR's client advertises 10-bit for the platforms it recognises, Pico included), full colour range, ALVR's 'Light' foveation preset (centre 0.80 x 0.80, edge ratio 8 x 8: nearly the whole view at full resolution); chroma-key passthrough is off by default (the setup offers it, key colour pure green #00FF00). Panel 2160 x 2160 per eye.
90 Hz has to be enabled in the Pico's own display settings first; if the headset only offers 72 Hz the wizard uses the closest rate it reports.
ALVR's wiki (Settings tutorial, v20): HEVC at a constant 100-150 Mbps on a good wireless router; this profile uses 150 Mbps (100 on an average network).

ALVR 20.14 added Pico 4 Ultra support (controller profile fix). Pico Neo 3 (XR2 Gen 1, 1832 x 1920) has no profile of its own: use this one and set the resolution in the wizard. Starting point, NOT verified by the AirFrameXR project on this headset.
